entries.title: Van Hollen Says Senators Aren’t Publicly Supporting Him Due to Fear of Schumer ‘Retaliation’
entries.summary: A number of Senate Democrats said Monday they were waiting to have a debate with the rest of the caucus before announcing their pick for majority leader.
entries.content:
Most Democratic senators are publicly staying neutral on the race for majority leader between Chuck Schumer and his challenger, Sen. Chris Van Hollen.

Only four members of the Democratic caucus have publicly stated their support for Van Hollen so far: Sens. Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont), Jeff Merkley (D-Oregon), and Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Michigan) and Peggy Flanagan (D-Minnesota), with many more demurring on Monday night. But Van Hollen thinks he has more support from his colleagues than is known and attributes their silence to a fear of angering Schumer.

“What you've got obviously is somebody who has the power of incumbency and so there is an element of concern about political retaliation,” the Maryland Democrat told The Washington Sun. “So it's hard to ask people to be public when they're worried that it will lead to bad consequences.”

Around 15 senators are supporting Schumer — still short of the close to 30 votes required to be reelected Democratic leader.

Van Hollen disputed reports that Schumer had already locked up the race to become leader.

“There was some article that came out that listed a bunch of people as having committed to Schumer, where I know for a fact some have said they're voting for me, and others I know are undecided on that list,” Van Hollen said Monday, insisting that he has a path.

The 67-year-old progressive senator has pitched himself as a change candidate who backs more aggressive tactics to end the Iran war and cut off U.S. aid to Israel. He’s also been critical of Schumer for wading into contested Democratic primary fights this year and for his stance opposing President Barack Obama’s nuclear deal with Iran.

Many of his colleagues say they’d welcome a discussion about leadership changes but credit Schumer with flipping as many as nine Senate seats in the midterm elections.

“We just had the single greatest results in a midterm election in a generation, and Leader Schumer was central to a lot of the recruitment and fundraising,” Sen. Chris Coons (D-Delaware) told The Sun. He described Van Hollen’s chances of becoming leader as “remote.”

Even Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, the junior senator from Maryland, declined to take a position on Van Hollen’s leadership bid.

“We’re going to have a big, big discussion tomorrow. We'll figure it out,” Alsobrooks said.

Sen. Mazie Hirono of Hawaii was the only Democrat who made news in announcing her support for leader as senators returned to Washington for a pair of votes on Monday.

“I have a long history with Chuck. He's helped me on some pretty necessary things that are really important to Hawaii,” Hirono told reporters.

Others, like Sen. Tim Kaine (D-Virginia), laid out the case for both sides.

“No one who was not on the ballot worked harder for this victory than Chuck Schumer. Chuck Schumer also happens to know Donald Trump better than anybody else in Congress,” Kaine said, though he added that “the voters are also overwhelmingly demanding change.”



Democratic senators also poured cold water on the idea of moving up the vote instead of holding it on Dec. 1, as originally scheduled, to help Schumer. Allies of the Democratic leader were reportedly pushing to hold an earlier vote.

“I haven’t heard that seriously proposed,” Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Georgia) said. “But I would oppose expediting before we've had a full process.”

And since the vote will take place via secret ballot, the public may never know how some senators voted.

“I am not telling one way or the other,” said Sen. Cory Booker (D-New Jersey), who’s considering a 2028 presidential bid. “It's a secret ballot.”
entries.author: Igor Bobic, Chase Pellegrini de Paur

entries.title: Ecuadorian Fishermen Injured in Drone Attack Sue the Trump Administration
entries.summary: The crew said the March attack sank their fishing boat and severely burned two men. They’re asking a federal judge to halt lethal U.S. boat strikes in the Pacific and Caribbean.
entries.content:
A crew of Ecuadorian fishermen sued the Trump administration Monday, alleging that drones launched from an American vessel sank their fishing boat in the Pacific Ocean and left two crew members with severe burns.

The lawsuit filed in the Western District of Pennsylvania seeks damages and an order ending lethal U.S. boat strikes in the Pacific and Caribbean. It gives grisly, firsthand details of the crew of La Negra Francesca Duarte II, who say the United States tortured and mocked them after misidentifying them as narcotics traffickers.

“Jordy’s leg was burned to the bone, and he bled profusely,” the complaint says of crew member Jordy Flores Lucas. “As a result of this attack, La Negra Francesca Duarte II was totally engulfed with flames and destroyed. The U.S. then kidnapped the surviving fishermen and held them against their will for around 24 hours.”

The Trump administration has claimed responsibility for carrying out missile and drone strikes — attacks the military argues target "narco-terrorists" in the Pacific — but has declined knowledge and responsibility for the attack on La Negra Francesca Duarte II and other Ecuadorean vessels destroyed earlier this year.

The fishermen say the Ecuadorian navy cleared their boat after a three-hour inspection shortly before the March 17 attack.

Following the bombardment, the crew escaped in small boats and approached a nearby ship, where armed personnel gave Flores Lucas medical care and zip-tied and hooded the others, according to the suit. The fishermen allege they were then “forced to stand barefoot on the iron deck which was very hot” and later taken to El Salvador where they were held against their will.

Flores Lucas recalled that military personnel showed him a drawing of the attack and “laughed about what they had done and about how they had destroyed the fishing vessel.”

The lawsuit alleges their treatment in U.S. custody amounted to torture, adding that the government has carried out the strikes without congressional authorization.

Last December, Democratic Reps. Jamie Raskin and Ted Lieu asked the Justice Department to investigate whether a separate Caribbean strike that killed survivors clinging to wreckage amounted to a war crime or murder.
entries.author: Gavin J. Quinton

entries.title: Huang Scandal Casts a Shadow Over Trump’s Asia Trip
entries.summary: Experts say the fallout from the Nvidia CEO’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy will affect the dynamics between the countries during this week’s talks.
entries.content:
The specter of Jensen Huang looms over President Donald Trump’s trip to Asia this week, as tensions over China’s involvement in the affair that led to Huang’s resignation from Nvidia threaten to overshadow historic trilateral talks on denuclearization.

“This does ramp up pressure on export controls and other things that China would view as provocative,” said a former Trump senior trade official, who, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe internal dynamics. “There's an open question about how this story will impact that broader dynamic and whether it inflames the relationship.”

The dynamic between the two global superpowers remains in an effective truce that both sides have described as strategic stability — built on the idea that neither party will drastically change the status quo without informing the other, to protect access to critical resources and temper flare-ups. While Trump hopes to maintain the equilibrium during his trip, the fallout from Huang’s apparent career implosion could complicate that goal.

“There were two different views,” Trump told reporters Monday when asked who is to blame for the growing scandal. “One view is, you don't want to insult China. We have a very good relationship with China, and you don't want to insult them. And the other view is just go, you know, down and dirty and do what you have to do. ... Can't say either is wrong or right. We'll let you know.”

Administration officials, AI lobbyists and national security experts said they expect the fallout from the scandal and Huang’s subsequent resignation to shake up the underlying dynamics of the summit in China, which is scheduled to include a meeting between Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin — and potentially with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

Trump left for Asia on Monday for a multiday trip, during which he will visit the Philippines for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit before flying to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.

Trump’s one-on-one meeting with Xi will be the leaders’ second bilateral in as many months, following Xi’s visit to Washington in September. It follows a midterm election that tilted political power away from the U.S. president, leaving him potentially weakened on the international stage during his lame-duck period. Trump and Xi could meet again next month when the U.S. hosts G20 leaders at a conference.

But this week, Trump is expected to discuss the trade truce with China that was agreed to in October 2025 and was extended in September — a deal that administration officials say China is not fully honoring.

Trump indicated Monday that he hadn’t determined whether he’ll confront Xi about his government’s role in the circumstances that led to Huang’s ouster, saying that he “may” ask Xi about the allegations that China used business executive Alice Huang to spy on Huang and Nvidia.

“I don’t know that she is a spy,” Trump said of Alice Huang, adding that “any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say, ‘She’s a spy.’”

“Nobody’s proven that she’s a spy,” Trump said. “She may not be a spy.”

Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company affiliated with Alice Huang, placed orders worth billions of dollars with Nvidia for top-of-the-line AI chips. The chips were subsequently acquired by the Chinese, as a method of circumventing U.S. laws that ban China from receiving Nvidia’s most advanced chips.

The Trump administration hasn’t discussed — and doesn’t plan to discuss — American export controls in negotiations with China, a senior U.S. official said when asked how the Nvidia fallout could affect the summit, referring to American export controls as “national security matters.”

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” the senior U.S. official said. “We don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there.”

Even if Trump doesn’t address it with Xi directly, officials in Washington and Beijing are already maneuvering to deal with the consequences of the situation. Congressional lawmakers are pushing for legislation to further regulate the sale of advanced AI chips to China, pressuring the Trump administration to restrict which technology American companies can sell abroad.

China’s Ministry of Commerce has warned against any actions that would disrupt Chinese manufacturing.

“The wind is at the back of China hawks right now,” said a national security expert, who spoke on the condition of anonymity for fear of reprisals in his private-sector work. “Jensen’s fall from grace is going to have a huge impact on congressional debates.”

And those who want stricter policy toward China — including some in the Trump administration — are better positioned because of it. The Washington Sun previously reported that China hawks are gaining momentum to include much stricter limits on chip exports in a defense bill set to move through Congress.

Senior government officials have begun internal conversations about accelerating export controls, aimed at getting ahead of an expected push from Congress, according to two other sources familiar with the matter, who also spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe private conversations.

Huang controversy aside, administration officials said the central focus of Trump’s meeting with Xi will be the implementation of the Busan trade agreement.

China has slow-walked delivery of the rare earth minerals that it agreed to provide to the U.S., the officials said, causing frustration within the administration and a hesitation to again extend the agreement.

“We’ve been quite public that, while we are getting rare earths and derivative products from the Chinese, we’re not getting them at the pace and at the level that we would like to be receiving them at,” said the senior U.S. official.

Another administration official gave a blunt description of the state of China’s deliveries.

“We are getting restricted on things that are critical for our development and military,” they said.

The trade agreement is scheduled to expire in January.

After Trump and Xi meet, Putin will join the pair for an equally anticipated conversation, which will include a discussion about the Iran war but is intended to address China’s emphasis on nuclear weapons. The trilateral meeting was first floated earlier this year, and Trump previously expressed being open to it.

China has been modernizing its nuclear arsenal for years at a dizzying rate that surpasses both the United States’ and Russia’s efforts to update their weapons. Experts have questioned the purpose of the rapid advancements, asking whether China’s nuclear philosophy is evolving into less of a defensive posture.

The meeting, a China policy expert said, could lead to better communication between the three nuclear powers.

“The best we can start hoping for is just building blocks,” the China policy expert said, “for some of these nuclear forces talking to one another, so that if there is an incident, it doesn’t escalate unnecessarily."
entries.author: Ben T.N. Mause, Jasmine Wright

entries.title: Iran Fires Drones At a U.S. Radar Facility In Bahrain
entries.summary: It's the third day of Iranian attacks on U.S. targets in the region since a roughly two-month lull.
entries.content:
By David Rising and Amir-Hussein Radjy

Iran fired drones across the Persian Gulf on Tuesday at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, its third attack in recent days on American military targets in the tiny island kingdom as Tehran resumed strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull.

After issuing an alert about the incoming fire, Bahrain said that its air defense systems had successfully intercepted the “treacherous Iranian aerial attacks.”

The attacks on American infrastructure in Bahrain are part of an evolution in Iran's strategy from waiting for an attack and then retaliating to targeting the operational capability of bases, Tehran-based security analyst Mostafa Najafi said.

“Tehran has shifted toward a more active, preemptive strategy — one focused on countering threats during their very formative stages,” he told The Associated Press.

Tuesday's attack came after the U.S. military's Central Command confirmed that the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group had arrived in the region. The move adds a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the American presence as U.S. President Donald Trump keeps his options open for his next move in the war, which began nearly nine months ago.

The combined U.S. naval assets in the Gulf, Arabian Sea, Red Sea, and Mediterranean now exceed the force deployed when the U.S. and Israel conducted joint strikes on Iran to launch the war on Feb. 28 — the presence provides greater offensive firepower and missile interception capacity, according to a new analysis by Israel's Institute for National Security Studies.

The Roosevelt joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as smaller U.S. Navy ships, which are in the region to maintain a blockade of Iranian shipping. U.S. Central Command wouldn't comment on whether it plans to keep all three carrier strike groups in the region or replace the Washington, which had been redeployed from the Asia-Pacific region to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln amid concerns of its lengthy deployment.

The Washington itself has now been deployed for around six months.
entries.author: The Associated Press
